title: Core Components Functional Blocks

cards.question: What is the role of memory in an AI agent's intelligence?
cards.answer: Memory acts as the storage system, allowing the agent to retain past states, successful actions, and 'world knowledge,' thereby providing context for future actions.

cards.text: Memory enables an agent to retain past states and {{successful actions}} for future reference.
cards.hint: Key outcomes that inform future decisions

cards.question: How does pattern recognition contribute to an AI agent's functionality?
cards.answer: Pattern recognition allows an AI agent to identify regularities in data, such as discerning a 'face' or a 'red block' from complex input, which is crucial during the perception phase.

cards.question: Which functional component allows an AI agent to improve by analyzing past successes and failures?
cards.explanation: Learning enables the agent to improve over time by updating internal models based on past experiences.

cards.question: What fundamental ability does inference give to an AI agent?
cards.answer: Inference allows an AI agent to make logical leaps, drawing new conclusions from existing knowledge and current observations.

cards.question: In the context of a robot vacuum learning to avoid a problematic rug, which component is most responsible for this improved behavior?
cards.explanation: Learning allows the vacuum to modify its behavior based on past experiences of getting stuck under the rug, improving future performance.

cards.text: {{Inference}} is the ability that empowers agents to draw new conclusions from existing knowledge and observations.

cards.question: What do syntactics and semantics represent in the context of AI language processing?
cards.answer: Syntactics refer to the formal rules, grammar, and structures (the 'how'), while semantics pertain to meaning, intent, or 'truth' (the 'why' and 'what').

cards.question: Why are modern AI systems challenged by semantics, despite being excellent syntacticians?
cards.answer: Modern AI systems excel at syntactics because they can flawlessly follow rules and grammar, but struggle with semantics as it involves understanding meaning and context beyond symbol manipulation.

cards.text: {{Semantics}} is the actual meaning, intent, or 'truth' behind the symbols in communication.
cards.hint: Deals with meaning, not just structure.

cards.text: The {{Frame Problem}} involves using syntax to represent common-sense changes in the real world.
cards.hint: A conceptual issue in AI related to representing change.

cards.question: What is an example of something that is syntactically correct but semantically nonsensical?

options.A: The sun sets in the west.
options.B: The diameter of a circle is twice its radius.
options.D: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius under standard conditions.

cards.explanation: The sentence 'Colorless green ideas sleep furiously' follows grammatical rules but lacks logical meaning.

cards.question: How is a localized 2D bounded region created using sigmoid neurons?
cards.answer: A localized 2D bounded region is created by using sigmoid neurons to define a hyperplane for each boundary of the region and then using an output layer neuron to perform an 'AND' operation on these boundaries.

cards.text: A single multi-input [[Sigmoid Neuron]] defines a {{hyperplane}} that separates the high-output region from the low-output region.

cards.question: What operation is used to combine the outputs of the boundary neurons when creating a 2D bounded region?
cards.explanation: The 'AND' operation ensures the output neuron fires high only when the input point is on the correct side of all four boundaries simultaneously.

cards.question: What is the purpose of using four separate hidden neurons when forming a 2D bounded region?
cards.answer: Four separate hidden neurons are used to define the four boundaries of a rectangular box to enclose a high-output region in 2D space.

cards.text: To enclose a box in 2D space, {{four separate hidden neurons}} are needed to define its boundaries.

cards.question: What is achieved by summing many 2D tower functions, each with its own position and height?

options.C: Constructing a complex 3D surface that approximates any continuous 2D function

cards.explanation: Summing many of these 2D tower functions allows the network to approximate any continuous 2D function effectively.

cards.question: What is the primary role of the Ingestion layer in the system architecture?
cards.answer: The Ingestion layer involves collecting data through specialized niche feeds and broad-ranging newspaper feeds, conducting freshness and liveness audits, and pulling data hourly via cron jobs.

cards.text: In the Processing layer, articles are converted into structured data by removing duplicates and non-relevant content, and generating {{text-embedding-3-small}} vectors.

cards.question: How does the Personalization layer expand user preferences?

options.B: By gathering information during onboarding, then using an LLM to create a detailed user description
options.D: By manual user input every session

cards.explanation: The Personalization layer gathers professional and interest information from users during onboarding, then utilizes a Large Language Model (LLM) to expand this into an embedded user description.

cards.question: How does the Deduplication process work in the Processing layer?
cards.answer: Deduplication removes duplicate articles through URL normalization, title similarity using Jaccard index, and cosine embedding similarity.

cards.text: The Delivery layer records user interactions for feedback events, which influence {{personalization}} by updating the user vector.

cards.question: What function does the theme classification in the Processing layer serve?

options.A: It filters out sponsored content and non-English articles
options.B: It assigns structured data into one of 17 themes based on embedding similarity to theme centroids
options.C: It normalizes URLs to prevent duplicates
options.D: It boosts article recency during personalization

cards.explanation: Theme classification in the Processing layer categorizes articles into 17 themes using embedding similarity to predefined theme centroids.

cards.question: How does feedback flow in the described system architecture?
cards.answer: Feedback flows upward from the Delivery layer to the Personalization layer, allowing user interactions to inform and refine user preferences.
